name: Wasp Rules Are Directional — Must Define Both Directions

solution.brief: Wasp rules are directional; create two separate Wasp_Rule components (A→B and B→A) for bidirectional part connections.
solution.principle:
Wasp_Rule encodes a directed graph edge, not an undirected one. The aggregation engine only permits connections matching the exact source→target direction specified, so symmetry must be explicitly declared by doubling rules in both orientations.

Related insight: The connection IDs that Wasp_Rule references are determined by the sequential input order into Wasp_Connection From Direction. Each connection plane is defined by a center point (origin) and a direction curve (X-axis). Reordering inputs changes IDs, which silently breaks rule references — a common source of aggregation failures.

Related insight: Related insight: Wasp_Rule references connection indices using 0-based numbering. When defining the two rules for a bidirectional connection, the indices are 'swapped' — if A's connection 0 mates with B's connection 1, the reverse rule uses B's connection 1 mating with A's connection 0. Misremembering that indices are 0-based (not 1-based) is a silent failure point.

Related insight: Related insight: The directional rules defined here feed into Wasp_Stochastic Aggregation as required inputs. The aggregation component is stateful and additive — it uses these rules each step to randomly select valid connections and grow the assembly incrementally. Incomplete rule sets (missing one direction of a bidirectional pair) will silently limit growth to one direction only.

intents: how do I make parts connect in both directions in Wasp
my Wasp aggregation is sparse or asymmetric
why are some connections not forming in stochastic aggregation
I want two parts to connect to each other bidirectionally
Wasp aggregation not using all connection points
symptoms: aggregation produces fewer connections than expected or looks sparse
parts only connect in one orientation but not the reverse
some connection indices are never used during aggregation
aggregation result is asymmetric despite symmetric geometry

preconditions: Using Wasp plugin for discrete aggregation
At least one Wasp_Rule component is defined connecting two part connections
Stochastic Aggregation or similar Wasp aggregation component is being used
User expects parts to connect symmetrically or bidirectionally

evolution_history.changes: Wasp_Rule references connection IDs, and those IDs come from sequential ordering in Wasp_Connection From Direction. This is a critical gotcha: the directionality of rules depends on correctly ordered connection IDs upstream.
New pattern explicitly introduces '0-based connection indices' and 'swapped-index' framing for bidirectional rules — specific details not yet present in this neighbor's context.

The new pattern's description of how aggregation consumes rules and grows incrementally adds useful downstream context to this pattern about directionality, reinforcing why both directions must be defined.
